title: Context, Trust Labels and Abstention in a Governed Text-to-SQL Layer: A Pre-registered Evaluation on an Insurance Warehouse (paper, question sets, run reports and analysis)
description:
Everything behind the paper Context, Trust Labels and Abstention in a Governed Text-to-SQL Layer: A Pre-registered Evaluation on an Insurance Warehouse (Kondapaka, 2026, preprint v1): the paper (analysis/insurance-2026-09-29/paper/paper.pdf), the benchmark harness, all five question sets with reference answers, every run report, the human audits, the set-5 pre-registration with its SHA-256 sealing hashes, the statistics script and the paper generator.

DQL is the open-source engine of ZLens (https://zlens.app). In a pre-registered test on 200 answerable questions written by a GPT model, DQL with modeled context answered 87.5% correctly with Claude Sonnet 5.5, against 59.5% for one-shot SQL and 80.5% for an agent given the same modeling knowledge as text (+7.0 points, exact McNemar p = 0.02); the difference from that agent vanishes under a grade that forgives label columns. Answers labelled governed at the dbt-metric levels were right in 36 of 54 cases, short of the pre-registered 95%.
